Instant Strike - An alternative to Steel Wind Strike!
Hey all! I'd just like to present a new spell to ask for criticism and advice!   


So, I've always liked Steel Wind Strike in terms of flavor. It's such a cool "anime"-esque thing to do. *Just imagine a Ranger or Eldritch Knight taking a deep breath, as he unsheathes his magical, glowing blade. Swift slashes of glimmering light follow, and in an instant . .  the warrior is now on the other side of the horde of enemies. The world stands still for a split second, and then you see the entire enemy force fall apart like jenga pieces . . . .*

Cool, right?   


My problem with it though, is that **it simply doesn't play out that way.** It's a 5th level spell, so Rangers only get it by tier 4 and 1/3rd casters can't even attain it, and it being a spell attack means that Rangers won't be much good at it anyway. This spell's best use is actually on a regular old Wizard, who gets to dump spell attack force damage and choose not to teleport. At that point, it might as well be "Magic Missile Armada"! Listen, I love Wizards - they're one of my favorite classes, but give the Martials some love too!   


So, here's my solution.   


**Instant Strike**

 2*th-level conjuration* 

 **Casting Time:** 1 action  
**Range:** 30 feet  
**Components:** S, M (a weapon worth at least 1 sp)  
**Duration:** Instantaneous 

 Your weapon weapon glows with arcane energy, as you instantly attack with impossible swiftness.  Choose up to three creatures you can see within range.  Make a weapon attack with the weapon used in the casting against each target, ignoring limitations set by the reach or range of your weapon.  On a hit, in addition to the weapon's damage, the target takes an additional 1d10 force damage. You then teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 5 feet of one of the targets you hit or missed.   


 ***Spell Lists.*** [Ranger](http://dnd5e.wikidot.com/spells:ranger), [Wizard](http://dnd5e.wikidot.com/spells:wizard)   


So, what do you all think? Broken? Underpowered? Abuse cases? Any suggestions or comments you'd like to make? I'm all ears.
